Where Do We Go Beyond Crafting?

It's just another trend, like graphics of the 80s. Realism of the 90s. Upgrades of the 00s. Crafting of the 10s. And a dozen smaller trends inside these times. Likely the next one will be immersion as it's been building on the horizon for a while and we can't really get game that much more realistic due to animation and processing restrictions, so now we look instead to behaviours and physics to makes a game feel more cohesive.

How do you feel VR devices like Oculus Rift will impact immersion? Honestly, I think it's going to be a tough sell to the consumer. I've seen it demoed several times and half the people that try it get motion sickness.

I*n regards to crafting mechanics, when it's done really well, it is quite immersive and makes for a great game experience. I really like the way it is handled in Don't Starve. The problem is so many developers attaching gathering/hoarding/crafting mechanics to their games for the sole purpose of getting people to play them longer.

VR needs a hell of a lot more work before the average person will be interested. Developing for VR is a pain in the arse and the market is tiny in comparison to even the smallest gaming markets. Immersion wise it's pretty good, but the limited scope with no feedback makes it hard to use for a lot of games.
